## Investigation Report

### Verdict / Confidence / Severity / Task Type

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Verdict | Confirmed |
| Confidence | High |
| Severity | Medium (P2) |
| Task type | Correctness / recovery |

### What Was Claimed

Issue #120 carries the `workflow-correctness-002` finding from PR #117: when merge fails after the issue has been projected as `workflow:awaiting-merge`, rollback to `workflow:in-review` is best-effort and tied to an abortable operation. A failed or cancelled rollback is suppressed, so an unmerged PR can retain the misleading awaiting-merge label.

### What We Found

The current parent-owned merge node in `src/workflows/work-on.ts` performs one compensating label update in the merge `catch` block and then uses `.catch(() => undefined)` before rethrowing the merge error. The projector's label update is a two-request GET/PUT sequence. The main merge request receives `ctx.signal`; rollback needs a separate bounded compensation path so cancellation of the primary operation cannot cancel the corrective label write. Transient rollback failures also need retry evidence rather than silent suppression.

The source already omits `ctx.signal` at this call site, but it still has the underlying correctness gap: rollback is one-shot and all failures are discarded. The fix must make the independence explicit and test the aborted-primary-operation case, rather than relying on an incidental omitted argument.

### Root Cause

The merge failure path treats rollback as an optional notification instead of a compensating side effect. It neither guarantees an independent rollback signal nor reports exhaustion when the label restoration cannot be confirmed. The outer node failure therefore has no reliable projection correction.

### Affected Files

- `src/workflows/work-on.ts` — merge failure compensation and reusable rollback seam.
- `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts` — focused regression coverage for cancellation-safe rollback and retry behavior.

### Evidence

- `src/workflows/work-on.ts:2164-2173`: merge catch invokes `setWorkflowLabel` once and suppresses every rollback error.
- `src/adapters/github-projection.ts:177-214`: `setWorkflowLabel` accepts an optional signal and performs GET then PUT.
- `test/adapters/github-projection.test.ts:73-108`: existing label projection coverage does not exercise abort/cancellation or compensating retries.
- `src/core/artifact-protocol.ts`: `workflow:awaiting-merge` and `workflow:in-review` are distinct projections and must not be conflated.

### History Findings

Issue #120 records the source PR #117 finding `workflow-correctness-002` at reviewed head `fbdfb397b88b22a8819e1d8fab53013f1f309`. The current frozen integration base is `89f2fa1c7e7020b695803e9a1b556d55076f2302`; no additional local history artifact is needed to reproduce the cited control-flow defect.

### Recommendation

Keep the change inside the merge compensation path. Add a small cancellation-safe rollback helper that uses a dedicated compensation signal and retries the label restoration, preserves the original merge error when rollback succeeds, and surfaces rollback exhaustion instead of silently hiding it. Add focused tests with an aborted primary signal and a fake projector that verifies a live independent signal and retry count.

### Related Issues

- Source PR: `#117`
- Source issue: `#92`
- Current remediation issue: `#120`
- Finding: `workflow-correctness-002`

### Decomposition Assessment

No decomposition is warranted. The defect is localized to one merge failure compensation path and one focused test surface; no product, API, UX, or security-authority decision is required.

### Acceptance Spec

- [ ] Merge-failure rollback cannot inherit an already-aborted primary signal.
- [ ] Rollback retries bounded transient failures and does not silently discard exhaustion.
- [ ] The primary merge error remains the reported cause when rollback succeeds.
- [ ] Focused regression coverage validates the aborted-signal scenario and retry behavior.
- [ ] No unrelated workflow, label vocabulary, or merge-authority behavior changes.

<!-- INVESTIGATION:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:CONTRACT -->
## Builder Contract

### Objective

Restore `workflow:in-review` after an unsuccessful merge attempt without allowing cancellation of the primary merge operation to cancel its compensating label update. Retry the bounded rollback and preserve failure evidence.

### Allowed Paths

- `src/workflows/work-on.ts` — merge failure compensation helper and call site.
- `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts` — focused cancellation and retry regression coverage.

### Forbidden Changes

- Do not change merge authorization, reviewed SHA/base validation, branch policy, or merge method.
- Do not change workflow label names or the normal label projection lifecycle.
- Do not add GitHub credentials, raw shell commands, arbitrary GitHub writes, or new workflow phases.
- Do not modify files outside the two allowed paths.
- Do not weaken fail-closed behavior when rollback cannot be confirmed.

### Invariants

- A rollback never uses the primary merge operation's already-aborted signal.
- The rollback attempts at most three label restorations and reports exhaustion.
- When rollback succeeds, the original merge failure remains the thrown failure.
- The compensating target is exactly `workflow:in-review`.
- Merge success behavior and durable merge evidence remain unchanged.
- Tests remain deterministic and do not contact GitHub or include private data.

### Deliverables

- Explicit `rollbackAwaitingMergeLabel` helper with independent compensation cancellation and bounded retries.
- Merge catch path wired to the helper without swallowing rollback failures.
- Regression tests covering an aborted primary signal, a live rollback signal, retries, and original-error preservation.

### Acceptance Mapping

| Check | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Cancellation-safe rollback | Dedicated rollback signal is created independently of the primary merge signal and passed to each label update. |
| Bounded retry | Helper retries transient/unknown projector failures no more than three times. |
| Failure evidence | Exhausted rollback throws an error containing the rollback failure while retaining the merge error as cause/context. |
| Regression coverage | `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts` fake projector asserts signal state, target label, retry count, and thrown error behavior. |
| Scope safety | Diff is limited to the two allowed paths; `npm run check` is the required verification. |

### Out of Scope

- Guaranteed recovery from total GitHub outage.
- Changes to `GitHubIssueProjector` request semantics or global projection retry policy.
- Changes to direct-run merge orchestration, CI gates, or parent-owned merge authority.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT -->
## Implementation Context

### History

Issue #120 is the remediation of PR #117 finding `workflow-correctness-002`; the frozen integration base is `89f2fa1c7e7020b695803e9a1b556d55076f2302`. The current source has a one-shot, swallowed rollback in the parent-owned merge node.

### Callers and Data Flow

1. Decision completion projects `workflow:awaiting-merge` after review gates pass.
2. The parent-owned merge node calls `mergePullRequest` with `ctx.signal`.
3. A merge rejection enters the catch block.
4. The catch must restore `workflow:in-review` before propagating the merge failure.
5. Reconciliation records the merge node failure; the label must not falsely indicate pending merge authority.

### CI Surface

`.forge/config.json` defines the required named local check `check` (`npm run check`), with GitHub CI required by policy after PR preparation. No additional verification command is authorized.

### Prior Findings

The source finding identifies the same abortable signal and `.catch(() => undefined)` as the cause of a stale `workflow:awaiting-merge` projection. The current implementation's omitted signal is incidental and untested; the contract makes signal independence explicit and removes silent rollback loss.

### Hazards

- A rollback GET/PUT can fail after the merge request has already been accepted or while the primary signal is aborted.
- Retrying an unknown merge is unsafe; only the label compensation is retried.
- Swallowing rollback exhaustion hides a stale projection and prevents durable reconciliation from explaining it.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT -->
## Implementation Plan

1. Add a small exported/testable helper in `src/workflows/work-on.ts` that creates one independent bounded compensation signal, calls `setWorkflowLabel` for `workflow:in-review`, retries up to three times, and throws a combined error if all attempts fail.
2. Replace the merge catch's one-shot swallowed call with the helper while rethrowing the original merge error after successful compensation.
3. Add focused unit tests in `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts` using a fake projector: abort the primary signal, assert every rollback signal is live and the label is correct, verify retry success, and verify exhausted rollback is surfaced.
4. Run the required named `check` verification and inspect the assigned diff for contract compliance.

### Risk Controls

- Keep the helper private in behavior and narrow in input shape; no adapter or policy changes.
- Clear any compensation timeout after success/failure so tests and the host do not retain timers.
- Preserve the merge error as the primary error when rollback succeeds; include both errors when compensation exhausts.
